questions.stem: A scientist treats cells with a drug that disrupts ribosome function. Which process would be most directly affected?

options.text: Cell division
Protein synthesis
Storage of genetic information
Osmosis across the cell membrane

questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis. Disrupting ribosome function would directly prevent the cell from making proteins, which are essential for almost all cellular processes.

questions.stem: A cell is observed to have a very high number of mitochondria. What can you infer about this cell?

options.text: It stores large amounts of starch
It is likely a bacterial cell
It has a high energy demand
It produces many lipids

questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration, which releases energy (ATP). A cell with many mitochondria, such as a muscle cell or sperm cell, requires a lot of energy to carry out its function.

questions.stem: A student examines a cell under a microscope and sees a nucleus, cell membrane, and cytoplasm, but no cell wall or chloroplasts. Which type of cell is it most likely to be?

options.text: A plant leaf cell
An animal cell
A bacterial cell
A plant root cell

questions.explanation: Animal cells have a nucleus, cell membrane, and cytoplasm but lack a cell wall and chloroplasts. Plant cells (including root cells) have a cell wall, and leaf cells also have chloroplasts. Bacterial cells lack a true nucleus.

questions.stem: A genetic disorder causes the cell membrane to become overly permeable. What is the most likely consequence for the cell?

options.text: The cell would produce more proteins
The cell would lose control over which substances enter and leave
The cell would divide more rapidly
The cell would increase in size permanently

questions.explanation: The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell. If it becomes overly permeable, the cell would lose this selective control, potentially allowing harmful substances in or essential molecules out, disrupting homeostasis.

questions.stem: A researcher removes the nucleus from an amoeba. The cell continues to move for a short time but eventually dies. Why does the cell die?

options.text: The cell can no longer perform respiration
The cell can no longer produce new proteins needed for survival
The cell immediately stops all chemical reactions
The cell membrane breaks down instantly

questions.explanation: The nucleus contains DNA, which carries the instructions for making proteins. Without a nucleus, the cell cannot produce new proteins (including enzymes), so existing proteins eventually break down and the cell dies. It survives briefly using proteins already made.
